g.text: 9 of 100 North Carolina counties raised their general rate from FY2021-22 to FY2025-26

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #333333

g.text: and 10 held it; the largest rise was Currituck, +16.0 cents per $100

text.style: font-size: 7px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: County general property tax rate, dollars per $100 of valuation. Open dot FY2021-22, blue dot FY2025-26; label = change in cents per $100.

text.style: font-size: 7px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: Sorted by size of change, largest first.

text.style: font-size: 7px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: Same rate scale ($0.225 to $1.00 per $100, all 100 counties) as the companion chart of counties that fell.

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: Source: hazeydata/openmillage data/nc-2021.csv and data/nc-2025.csv (body_type = county, one row per county; North Carolina Department of Revenue).

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: Unit basis: per $100 is stated by the source for FY2025-26 only; for FY2021-22 it is inferred (reference/nc_unit_basis.csv).

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: All 100 counties present in both years; none missing. 81 fell, 9 rose, 10 unchanged.

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: Rate drops often follow a county revaluation (rates fall when values are reassessed); revaluation years are not recorded in these files, so they are not marked.
